reviews.review: I will never understand any positive word said about this game. No. NO!!!! I tried as hard as possible. NO YOU CAN'T MAKE ME!! YOU WONT MAKE ME PLAY THIS TORTURE AGAIN!!!!

ME:A have the Best Combat Gameplay compared to the OG ME imo. Everthing else, feels stale.

Run it Vanilla, Then Mod It. 

https://youtu.be/Y07pPQjQB5Q

Surprised to discover Multiplayer still active. If you were a fan of ME3 MP, you'll won't find much novelty due to being pretty much the same on every gameplay aspect, with the plus of being able to jet jump. Its relevance on the main story however, is none. Some rewards are transferable to Single Player, and maybe some dialogue, but thats about it. 

Bought this game last year, have over 60h in it and still at 53% progression. When you think you cleared a zone, something will make you come back to it. Andromeda does not have the legendary cast like the main branch did, and the stakes - while also involving survival - are much different. Lovecraftian elements are still present though not critical in the same way. The formula adopted by Bioware will also feel way more familiar to Dragon Age Inquisition than the first ME, and you'll feel that quickly the moment you learn about the Revenant and their place in the story.

I am loving it. The bugs that plagued its launch are no longer present, or at least, the gamebreaking ones. You can find the odd helment disappearing when changing instances, but for me, has been about it. Even quests you find and solve by accident without a quest giver become resolved with a proper prompt, no longer pestering the quest log ad eternum. The cast is interesting though less larger than life, yet they grow on you. The missions are high quality standing on its own, with the main themes being colonialism (the good and the bad), xenophobia (where the milky way species are the invasive ones), survival and AI. I feel like this medium explores a lot of these themes better than some Max Tegmark or Yuval Harari. (I do not mean Andromeda's stories are "deep" either, but they do put you in the heart of theorized events).

What you don't have is the Paragon vs Renegade type of choices and I am glad for it. Your choices, overall, also do not seem to impact the endgame (which does not sit well, I admit) but they can alter the galaxy's state of affairs. You simply have to come to terms you're building your own Pathfinder attitude towards the mission, politics and personal commitments. Of course, you feel like you're building a coalition for the big battle, but the cliché simply fits here and it is clearer: it's about the journey.

Never late to come back to Andromeda, nor late to start it now completely fresh. I must say the game turned out for the better when I stopped comparing it to the main trilogy. Clinging to stuff that way does for a bad recipe. Unsure how this one will fit into future projects if we ever come back to new Mass Effect IPs, but I'm looking forward to it.
